title: Service-Fee Share Refunds on Cartwise Grocery Orders
content:
# Service-fee share refunds on Cartwise Grocery Orders

## The rule

The service fee billed on an order is shared back with its item refunds only once a price-protection or weight-overage refund stands on the order: from then on, on a service level whose setting for returning the service fee with item refunds is on, the service-fee share refund this rule computes is booked against the order's service fee charge with `refund_reason` `item_refund_share`; an order carrying only missing, damaged, wrong-item or quality refunds keeps its service fee.

The service-fee share refund is fixed only after the weight-overage refund owed on every line sold by weight and billed above its overage allowance stands on the order. The service-fee share refund is fixed only after the price-protection refund owed on every unapproved replacement billed above its protected price stands on the order.

Read as states of the order's entries: the figure of the service-fee share refund is settled only while each weight-overage refund owed on a line sold by weight, and each price-protection refund owed on an unapproved replacement, already stands among the order's entries.

## Points of judgement

| Item refunds standing on a Cartwise Grocery Orders order | Is the service fee shared back? |
|---|---|
| Only missing, damaged, wrong-item or quality refunds | No. The order keeps its service fee. |
| No price-protection refund and no weight-overage refund of any kind | No. |
| At least one price-protection refund | Yes, where the service level's setting for returning the service fee with item refunds is on. |
| At least one weight-overage refund | Yes, where that setting is on. |

The refund is a fee refund: it is booked against the order's service fee charge, not against an item line, and it lowers the net amount billed on the order.

## Booking tool: `refund_service_fee_share_1e350a8d`

**Capability.** The tool returns to the customer part of the service fee billed on a Cartwise grocery order, as the service-fee share that goes back with item refunds on that order. One call adds one fee-refund entry to the order for the service fee charge it names, with the reason "item refund share" and the refunded amount, paid to the customer's original payment method; the order's net billed amount falls by that amount. The fee refund shows at once among the order's entries with today's date.

**Invocation.** This is an agent-side tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it by its exact name, `refund_service_fee_share_1e350a8d`, through `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | The customer reference number of the person who placed the order, read from the customer profile lookup | Id |
| `order_id` | The order number of the grocery order whose service fee is partly returned, read from the order lookup | Id |
| `source_event_id` | The reference number of the service fee charge entry on that order that this refund pays back, read from the order entries lookup | Id |
| `amount_usd` | The amount of service fee returned | USD, a positive number with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before it is passed; never 0 or negative |

**Return.** A dictionary rendered as text with `order_event_id` (the reference number of the new fee-refund entry), `order_id` (the order refunded), `fee_type` (always `service`), `refund_reason` (always `item_refund_share`), `refund_destination` (always `original_payment_method`), `amount_usd` (the amount booked, USD with 2 decimal places) and `status` ("booked" when the fee refund now stands on the order).

**Hypothetical illustration.** A call naming a customer, an order, that order's service fee charge entry and an amount of 1.24 returns a receipt whose `fee_type` is `service`, whose `refund_reason` is `item_refund_share`, whose `amount_usd` is 1.24 and whose `status` is "booked".
